Require a PIN (or biometric) every time the app opens or returns from the background.
How long KyPost may stay in the background before it locks again. Picking a short window means switching to another app — the file picker, your browser, the camera — locks KyPost before you get back.
Enter your PIN to turn this off
No mail, contacts, or attachments are cached on this device — everything is fetched fresh from the server each time. Turning this on immediately wipes what\'s cached now and restarts the app.
Off by default. When on, the credential this device sends mail and answers sign-ins with is locked behind your PIN, and new-mail notifications show no sender or subject until you unlock the app.
Push always sends the sender and subject through Google/UnifiedPush relay servers, even with this on. For zero leakage, ask your server admin to switch this device to Pull mode instead.
This hides notification content while locked

While this is on, new-mail notifications show only that something arrived — no sender and no subject — until you open the app and enter your PIN. Sign-in approvals still arrive, but answering one needs your PIN, not just a fingerprint. Turn this on only if you understand that tradeoff.
Too many wrong PIN attempts. Local data on this device has been erased.
Too many wrong PIN attempts. Erasing local data did not finish; it will be retried when the app next starts.
Erasing local data did not finish and will not be retried automatically. Some data may still be on this device — reinstall the app to remove it.
KyPost could not unlock this device’s stored pairing credential, so the lock was left on. Nothing was deleted. Unpair and pair this device again, then try turning the lock off.

After this many wrong PINs in a row, KyPost erases the mail and contacts cached on this device, removes the contacts it synced to your phone, and unpairs this device. None of it can be recovered — KyPost deliberately keeps no backup.\n\nEach wrong PIN after the second one also delays the next attempt, up to an hour, so reaching the limit takes most of a day.
What happens after repeated wrong PINs. Erasing protects a lost or stolen phone; turning it off protects you from someone who just wants to cause damage.

This device’s secure storage could no longer be read, so KyPost had to reset it. This usually happens after a change to the device’s screen lock or a system update.

The key to the local mail database was stored there, so the cached copy of your mail and contacts could no longer be opened and has been deleted. Nothing on the server was touched — sync again to restore it.

You may also need to pair this device again, set your KyPost PIN again, and re-enrol this device for encrypted mail.
